This text is read-only, so it cannot be replaced: use Copy or Share. The selection menu carries text only (images go through Share); some phones show extra entries under the three dots.
Opens the Grabber panel when you select text in any app

Grabber on selection reads Android\'s text-selection events: the text of the view you select in, the selection range and the app\'s package name (it asks for window access only so a browser page can report which text is selected). It does not log the screen, your typing or password fields, and it never acts on another app. A steady selection opens the Grabber panel, which looks the text up (DuckDuckGo, OpenStreetMap, Wikipedia) like the selection-menu entry and keeps it in Recent grabs on this phone. It also needs the switch in Cloud Keyboard > Grabber > Text Selection, off by default.
Without accessibility, Android never lets an app react by itself to a selection. The free paths take one tap: the selection menu entry, or the assistant gesture (long-press the side or home button).
Selection menu: select text in any app, then pick Cloud Keyboard in the menu (under the three dots or More on Samsung and in Chrome).

Choose Cloud Keyboard in Settings > Apps > Default apps > Digital assistant app, and turn on Use text from screen and Use screenshot there. Then a long-press of the side or home button opens the screen text for picking, with no accessibility permission.
